A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same study, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 refers to an appendix that is absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of that supplementary material with v3 Appendices A-C.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, Stable Diffusion generation results, configuration comparisons and Grad-CAM visualizations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional personalization experiments, baseline comparisons and analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The filter decomposition, frozen coefficients, recursive atom expansion and linear-layer adaptation remain. The overcomplete initialization changes: v1 Section 5.2 specifies Kaiming-initialized coefficients and zero atom updates, whereas v3 Section 3.4 repeats the existing atoms and initializes beta to 1/m1. The expanded Kronecker explanation does not establish a separate new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds personalized text-to-image generation on 30 DreamBooth concepts and castle/canal case studies, including a castle example attributed to CustomConcept101. These introduce subject fidelity and generation under varied prompts as task requirements. The earlier VTAB, full CIFAR-100/ImageNet and CUB coverage remains; several experiments move to Appendix C.

E2.justification: v3 adds LoHa and LoKr to the retained VTAB generation comparison and BitFit to ConvNeXt classification. The new personalization comparison evaluates OFT, COFT, DiffFit and other methods beyond v1's principal LoRA/full-tuning comparisons. Appendix Table 8 additionally compares the method with Adapter, FacT and SSF on ViT.

E3.justification: The new personalization protocol uses 4-9 training images per concept, 1,000 tuning steps, 512-by-512 generation, 25 prompts, and DINOv2 fidelity, Vendi diversity and CLIP alignment metrics. v3 also evaluates ViT-B/16 and reports tuning beta, D1 and Dc for VTAB generation instead of v1's selected D/Dc configuration; unchanged FIDs do not establish a rerun. Revised validation settings are partly ambiguous because Section 4.2 specifies m1=3 and kc=2 where Table 1 labels m1=4 and kc=4.

E4.justification: v3 adds an ablation of freezing versus updating atom coefficients to investigate generalization and overfitting (Table 2 and Figure 5), plus configuration sensitivity comparisons for castle/canal generation. Appendix C extends Grad-CAM to additional blocks and images. The m=6/12 analyses were already mentioned in v1, so their appearance is not treated as evidence of a newly designed experiment.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. v3's additional metrics and result rows continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds personalization, ViT and baseline results. For example, Table 2 reports C2 diversity of 9.37 versus LoRA's 4.84, but lower fidelity, 0.652 versus 0.697, documenting a tradeoff. Most retained benchmark entries are unchanged, including the method's VTAB mean FID of 54.7. ConvNeXt Resisc45 accuracy changes from 86.4 to 87.6, while the reported mean remains 73.59; validation results also change.

T1.justification: v3 adds a mathematical completeness criterion for filter atoms and symbolic FLOP and parameter-count analyses in Appendix B. The main decomposition equations remain equivalent in substance, and the Kronecker formulation largely explains the existing block decomposition. Neither version supplies a theoretical guarantee or proof of the generalization claims.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes parameter efficiency, spatial structure and performance. v3 makes preserving pretrained capabilities and preventing overfitting through fixed atom coefficients an explicit contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. It also reframes filter decomposition as inspiration from prior research while retaining the efficient-tuning and recursive-expansion contributions.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive interpretations connecting coefficient updates with lost diversity and prompt alignment, and explains BitFit/DiffFit through their preservation of spatial filters and channel weights. It adds guidance about configuration-dependent capacity tradeoffs and explicitly identifies application to linear layers as underexplored. The earlier Grad-CAM interpretation is retained in Appendix C.

D1.justification: v3 supplies substantial information absent from the available v1 material: a stated project-code link, baseline implementation sources, the Stable Diffusion v1-4 checkpoint, dataset split counts and prompt templates. It newly specifies ISTA decomposition, coefficient reuse, execution without intermediate feature maps, and approximate GPU decomposition/training times. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified implementation choices.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises the research positioning by acknowledging DCFNet, filter-basis learning, convolutional sparse coding and prior filter-atom adaptation. It connects the approach to continual learning and multitask subspaces, and expands discussion of Kronecker adaptation and diffusion personalization. This changes attribution and motivation beyond adding citations for new experiments.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivation and method exposition are substantially rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, generative experiments precede discriminative experiments, and full-dataset classification and Grad-CAM discussion move into Appendix C. The narrative increasingly centers on spatial versus channel operations and preservation of pretrained capabilities.

P2.justification: v3 redraws and recombines the method diagrams, adds a linear-layer decomposition diagram, and replaces the main validation scatterplot with a numerical table. It adds concept-generation panels and comparison tables, reorganizes VTAB samples into expanded per-dataset grids, and enlarges the retained Grad-CAM presentation. These are substantial display changes beyond conference formatting and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's reliance mainly on LoRA comparisons: broader baselines, quantitative personalization tests and coefficient-freezing ablations address important questions about effectiveness and generalization. Clearer prior-work attribution and implementation disclosures also improve the paper. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including conflicting validation settings and inconsistent means in Tables 4 and 8. Those errors, absent uncertainty estimates and the differing parameter budgets in the coefficient ablation still limit precise performance and causal conclusions.
